claims.text: Instrumented nanoindentation complemented by micro-tensile testing can characterize the mechanical properties of as-processed FeNiCrMn HEA.
Local hardness and elastic modulus in FeNiCrMn HEA will be positively correlated with macroscopic yield strength and ductility.
The initial FeNiCrMn HEA is in an as-cast or annealed state optimized for corrosion resistance.
Instrumented nanoindentation will measure localized hardness and elastic modulus.
Micro-tensile testing will determine tensile strength, ductility, and yield behavior.
Room-temperature laboratory testing under controlled loading conditions is representative of service environments relevant to aerospace, energy, and automotive applications.
Grain size and phase-distribution heterogeneities may influence local mechanical responses in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Grain size and phase-distribution heterogeneities may influence global mechanical responses in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Nanoindentation quantifies small-scale elastic and plastic properties.
Micro-tensile testing captures overall deformation behavior.
Finer microstructural features produce higher local hardness and elastic modulus.
Regions with higher local hardness and elastic modulus contribute to improved macroscopic strength.
Regions with higher local hardness and elastic modulus contribute to improved macroscopic ductility.
Higher local hardness and elastic modulus will correspond to increased tensile strength and yield behavior.
Combining nanoindentation and micro-tensile testing will provide comprehensive mapping of local and global mechanical properties.
Existing research on FeNiCrMn HEA has primarily focused on corrosion resistance and provides limited mechanical-property data.
The proposed relationship may not apply after further thermomechanical processing or significant compositional modification.
